reviews.comment: I feel cheated by this guy. The class was supposed to be about embedded systems/microprocessors, but It didn't teach anything in a way that could be used in industry. All the concepts were taught on a rasbberry pi which does not prepare you for industry-level embedded systems Important topics in mcu design and functionality were very badly taught.

Just be glad he retired from teaching and hope the department won't let him teach another class again. 
 There is no usable study material for his exams as his notes look like chicken scratch. He is one of the rudest professors in the department. He plays favorites with his students; if you aren't one of the lucky ones, you won't get an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I believe that i developed a mental disorder from this class.

He has the driest humor out there, and will tell you your project sucks with everything that should be improved. In the moment, it is utterly miserable, but if you try he will give you a A or B. Exams are impossible and are not worth more than 4 hours of prep.

Doesn't make you aware of due dates for project deliverables until a couple days before, and therefore has no timeline for the semester. Lab assignments are not terrible, it is the project that sucks. Not willing to listen to your ideas, only believes what he wants to, and is overall subjective with how he grades your project. Avoid at all costs.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher overall, I don't get the ratings. Extra credit was always an option if you wanted to improve a low grade. Liu was very easy to access or message outside of class. I Came in after class several times and got 1-on-1 help to improve my work. I'm guessing the bad ratings are from students who didn't understand the material well enough.

Dr. Liu should be avoided at all costs. He very rarely actually teaches and the majority of lecture time is generally spent discussing how to organize and manage the class. The class itself is a mess, Liu has managed to make it incredibly disorganized. Project assignments are incredibly vague in their requirements and grades are critiqued harshly.

The lectures are random so the exams are hard. The labs can be frustrating but overall are not too bad. Most of your grade comes from the final project so make sure he likes you/your idea. He curves so you have no idea what you're going to get until grades post. He gives a lot of As and Bs though, so it's hard to get a C. Not a high workload.

would be a cool class if he wasn't so disorganized; lectures are all over the place and exams are difficult with low averages; would announce progress checks like less than a day in advance for our project; gave very little feedback and basically did not let us explain our own project
This guy sucks - he is rude and mean and a bad teacher

Lectures were impossible to follow and tests were graded on keywords he looked for with averages in the 50s. Feedback he gave was useless since he never returned tests, and on the final project, your grade hinged on his opinion of your project. If he thought it was too easy, he refused to give tips on how to improve it. Take ECEN 449 instead.

Liu is arguably one of the worst professors in the entire CS department. Not only is his class terribly disorganized; he is genuinely a very mean-spirited person. He openly harasses and insults his students. Avoid this man if at all possible. Group projects are a nightmare. You'll learn 0% about microprocessors and 100% about migraines.

Project-based class, but Dr. Liu constantly changes around the requirements. At the beginning of the final project, he approved our group's project proposal. However, when we made the final product exactly how we said we would, he deducted points for the project not being "complex enough". Subjective grading style and talks down to his students.

Would avoid at all costs, take ECEN 449 instead. Notes are a mess, has issues with recording lectures, is very passive-aggressive to his students when they ask about the unclear and changing requirements for the final project or any other coursework. Best part about this prof was when he called me retarded in front of the whole class.

Dr. Liu taught me microprocessor systems, however, I never learned one thing about microprocessors. His course is structured to where the final project will determine your grade and you will have no idea how you are doing in the class until it is too late to drop the course. He has also repeatedly antagonized my group members and me for no reason.

Your performance in his class is entirely dependent on how you perform on the final project. There is no clear grading criteria for the project and there is a heavy emphasis on presentation. Your grades before the project have little to no impact. His lectures are not informative. He spends lots of time trying to figure out technology.

Terrible professor. I would tell anyone not to take him if there were any other options out there. Prof can literally give you any grade he wants because of the way he's structured this class. Everything is subjective so there's no way to argue with him. Has told individual students that they are acting childish on multiple occasions. Take ECEN449.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is clearly the most useless class I have ever taken. Haven't learned a thing since day 1. This dude is the most b1p0lAr guy on the planet. Mans says my team's project is good and then later says that we need more technical discussions and a more complex project.He also yells at students constantly.Worst class/prof ever! If u c him, jump ship!

reviews.comment: Still don't have an understanding of what the course content, Microcomputer Systems, is. Bad lecturing, loose grade requirements, and overall just a bad experience. Sad that there is no other option out there.

reviews.comment: Great guy, terrible teacher. He enjoys teaching and wants to connect with his students, but lectures are hard to follow and it's hard to extract the important information from them. Grading criteria is subjective, so a good relationship with him will help you out. He is the most disorganized professor I've ever had, so join a group chat
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His lectures are difficult to follow and the course materials/notes are almost unusable. Unclear grading requirements for coursework and takes ages to receive grades. Micromanages students on projects and labwork. Most days he is authoritarian and grumpy, yet he has mood swings, so sometimes he isn't as irascible.

Love Dr. Liu! This class is fun in that it combines software and hardware concepts. Dr. Liu is very sweet, caring, and helpful. This class should not have exams since it is project based but not terrible. Dr. Liu is extremely hard working and really does his best to help everyone succeed

451 - RE - is an extremely difficult course and emotions tend to flare. The others are right, inconvenient changes were made. I was frustrated as well. However, I spoke openly with him and he listens. He honestly wants the best for all his students and only expects students try their best. The key is just work hard, show effort and you'll do well.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Doesn't give very clear requirements, and his lectures aren't very inspiring. It was impossible to tell what he wanted for homework and the group project.

Moves the goalpost on final project requirements even two days before the end of classes. No objective requirements for final project. Not enough grades in by q-drop that you could still easily fail the class. Doesn't even teach the class himself. Doesn't know the subject matter as much as he claims he does (can't answer most technical questions)
